title: This summer I'm going home
goal: Talk about plans and things that haven't happened yet, using the future tense.
bekal: form the future tense: *ólfaidh mé*, *ceannóidh mé*, *rachaidh mé*
use *ní* with séimhiú and *an* with urú, just as in the present
talk about plans with time words like *amárach, an tseachtain seo chugainn*

dialogs.title: Comhrá — Pleananna don samhradh
dialogs.intro: The end of the semester is near. Seán and Budi sit in the park talking about summer plans.

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.text: Cad a dhéanfaidh tú sa samhradh?
lines.id: What are you doing this summer?
lines.literal: what that will-do you in-the summer?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Rachaidh mé abhaile go dtí an Indinéis ar feadh míosa.
lines.id: I'll go home to Indonesia for a month.
lines.literal: will-go I homeward to the Indonesia for month-of.

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.id: Will you come back to Ireland?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Fillfidh, cinnte. Tosóidh an cúrsa nua i mí Mheán Fómhair.
lines.id: Definitely. The new course starts in September.
lines.literal: will-return, surely. will-start the course new in month September.

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.text: Cad a dhéanfaidh tú sa bhaile?
lines.id: What will you do at home?
lines.literal: what that will-do you in-the home?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Feicfidh mé mo theaghlach. Íosfaidh mé bia mo mháthar!
lines.id: I'll see my family. I'll eat my mother's cooking!
lines.literal: will-see I my family. will-eat I food my mother-of!

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.text: Ha! An dtabharfaidh tú rud éigin dom?
lines.id: Ha! Will you bring me something?
lines.literal: ha! question will-give you thing some to-me?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Tabharfaidh. Gheobhaidh mé caife maith duit.
lines.id: I will. I'll get you some good coffee.
lines.literal: will-give. will-get I coffee good to-you.

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.text: Go hiontach. Beidh mise ag obair anseo an samhradh ar fad.
lines.id: Great. Myself, I'll be working here all summer.
lines.literal: wonderful. will-be I at work here the summer on length.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: An mbeidh tú saor ag an deireadh seachtaine?
lines.id: Will you be free at the weekend?
lines.literal: question will-be you free at the end week-of?

lines.speaker: Seán:
lines.text: Beidh. Rachaimid go dtí an trá.
lines.id: I will. Let's go to the beach.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ceart go leor — ach ní rachaidh mé san uisce. Tá sé rófhuar!
lines.id: OK — but I won't go in the water. It's freezing!
lines.literal: right enough — but not will-go I in-the water. is it too-cold!

notes: **The future has its own endings, and the first letter is left alone.** The first conjugation adds **-faidh** (broad stem) or **-fidh** (slender stem): *ól* → *ólfaidh*, *cuir* → *cuirfidh*. The second conjugation adds **-óidh** or **-eoidh**: *ceannaigh* → *ceannóidh*, *imigh* → *imeoidh*. Unlike the past, there's no séimhiú and no *d'*.

**The f in these endings sounds like h.** *Ólfaidh* is said "OHL-hee", *fanfaidh* "FAN-hee", *tuigfidh* "TIG-hee". After a voiced sound it can sound like a light "w" or vanish completely. Don't pronounce it as a full f — that sounds like reading the spelling aloud.

**Ní brings séimhiú, an brings urú — exactly as in the present.** *Ní cheannóidh mé*, *an gceannóidh tú?*; *ní thuigfidh mé*, *an dtuigfidh tú?* So of the three tenses you've learned, only the past is the odd one out (there *ar* brings séimhiú too). When in doubt, remember: **the past softens everything; the other two follow the usual rules.**

**Rachaidh, gheobhaidh, íosfaidh — irregulars again.** *Téigh* becomes *rachaidh* (RAH-khee), which keeps not a single letter of the stem. *Faigh* becomes *gheobhaidh* (YOH-ee) in statements but *ní bhfaighidh* in the negative — the only verb whose stem switches between statement and negative. *Ith* becomes *íosfaidh* (EE-see).

blocks.text: The "we" form has its own ending: *ólfaimid*, *ceannóimid*, *rachaimid*. For other persons, just change the pronoun: *ólfaidh tú*, *ólfaidh sé*, *ólfaidh siad*.

blocks.title: How the future endings sound
items: *-faidh* and *-fidh* both sound like "hee": *ólfaidh* = OHL-hee, *cuirfidh* = KIR-hee, *fanfaidh* = FAN-hee.
Because the endings are long and lightly stressed, the Irish future is easy to pick out by ear once you know that "hee" sound.

blocks.title: Three future sentences you'll hear most
items: *Feicfidh mé thú* — "see you". You've used it since Unit 1 without knowing it was future.
*Rachaidh mé abhaile* — "I'll go home". Note that *abhaile* ("home, homeward") is different from *sa bhaile* ("at home").

blocks.text: For fixed plans, Irish often uses the *ag* pattern (Unit 9) instead of the future, just as English says "I'm going home tomorrow": *Tá mé ag dul abhaile amárach*. Both are correct; the future sounds a little more formal.

exercises.prompt: Put into the future tense ("I" form).
Make these sentences negative. Remember: *ní* brings séimhiú.
Turn these into questions. Remember: *an* brings urú.

items: Will you come back to Ireland?
Will you be free at the weekend?
I won't go in the water.

answers: ólfaidh mé — fanfaidh mé — tuigfidh mé — ceannóidh mé — tosóidh mé — imeoidh mé
Ní cheannóidh mé leabhar. — Ní fhanfaidh mé anseo. — Ní thuigfidh sé an cheist. — Ní ghlanfaidh sí an teach. — Ní rachaidh mé abhaile. — Ní bheidh mé saor amárach.
An gceannóidh tú bia? — An bhfanfaidh tú anseo? — An dtuigfidh tú é? — An mbeidh tú saor? — An dtiocfaidh tú amárach? — An ólfaidh tú tae?

Rachaidh mé abhaile sa samhradh. — An bhfillfidh tú go hÉirinn? — Tosóidh an cúrsa i mí Mheán Fómhair. — Feicfidh mé mo theaghlach. — An mbeidh tú saor ag an deireadh seachtaine? — Ní rachaidh mé san uisce.
